parts.text: Which claim places each structure correctly in the sequence cell, tissue, organ, organ system?

options.text: Muscle cell = cell; similar muscle cells together = tissue; heart = organ; circulatory system = organ system.
Similar muscle cells together = cell; the heart = tissue; circulatory system = organ.
Tissue combines to form cells, so the muscle cell sits above the tissue level.
The heart is an organism because it is large and keeps a person alive.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Vivaan lists four biological structures: a muscle cell, a bundle of similar muscle cells working together, the heart, and the circulatory system that includes the heart and blood vessels.

part_answers.answer: Organisation rises from one cell, to similar cells as tissue, to an organ made of tissues, to an organ system of organs working together; size alone does not make the heart an organism, and tissues do not build cells.

teacher.key_rationale: Cell → tissue → organ → organ system. Bundles of similar cells are tissue; the heart is an organ; the circulatory system is an organ system. Reversing tissue and cell, or treating a large organ as an organism, misses the sequence hinge.
